environment.host: Linux 6.17.0-42-generic, 16 cores (shard legs run in parallel per protocol)
environment.tree: git archive HEAD -> /tmp/j1-export (tracked files only, no .git; local build outputs excluded)

verdicts.verdict_note: verdicts DIFFER -> J1 FAIL per protocol. The merged PASS is vacuous: merged.json holds a 3-file scan surface (see rootCause 1). In the real workflow the merge-step set-completeness check exits 1 before adjudication runs, so this PASS could never be produced by CI - recorded to show that verdict equality alone would mask a broken scan surface (why completeness gates BEFORE adjudication).
verdicts.selftest_note: tcb_judgments selftest 12/12 fixtures passed - every judgment FAIL path is alive

timing.shard_wall_note: shard wall times are NOT a parallelization speedup: the shard scans dropped ~99.9% of their input files (rootCause 1) - the wall time reflects a near-empty scan, not half the work. The full scan (6568 files, 505s) is the only valid throughput measurement in this run.

scanReports.note: full/merged/shard0/shard1 scan reports (multi-MB) are not committed; sha256 recorded above. Evaluator outputs and projection maps are committed next to this summary.

rootCauses.title: shard file-list scan drops ~99.9% of input files (workflow shard topology cannot pass)
rootCauses.measured: shard0: 3288 input paths -> 2 file entries (topology.json, topology_policy.json); shard1: 3288 -> 1 (topology.lock); each shard report also carries the full 650-entry directory inventory
mechanism: xargs splits each shard list (~162,204 / ~162,188 bytes) into 2 scancode invocations because it exceeds the xargs default command buffer (131,072 bytes) - the workflow comment estimated ~115KB which fits kernel ARG_MAX (2,097,152) but not the xargs buffer; each later invocation overwrites --json-pp output of the earlier one (observed split: shard0 2515+773 args, shard1 2510+778 args; per-invocation scanned files 33+2 and 13+1)

ScanCode 32.5.0 converts a multi-file (>=2) input list into a scan of the common-prefix root ('.' for a tree-spanning list) with the input paths re-injected as --include patterns (scancode/cli.py:616-649, 'FIXME: support the multiple root better')

include matching (commoncode/fileset.py:101-148): patterns without '/' (root-level file names) are fnmatch-matched against path SEGMENTS - they hit any file with that basename at any depth (e.g. a 'README.md' arg matched 13 README.md files across the tree); patterns with '/' (subdirectory paths) are matched against the full resource path '<cwd-basename>/<repo-rel>' - the cwd-basename prefix ('j1-export/') is not in the pattern, so ALL subdirectory file args silently fail to match and are dropped, with exit 0

deterministic verification: a Python re-implementation of the include semantics predicted the per-invocation scanned-file counts and exact paths (shard0: 33+2, shard1: 13+1, e.g. batch2 = topology.json + topology_policy.json / topology.lock) - exact match with the measured reports

direct probes: 4 root-level file args -> 4 file entries scanned; 4 subdirectory file args -> 0 file entries scanned (exit 0); single-file arg scans the file but emits the bare BASENAME ('MIT.txt') with 0 directory entries; directory arg ('LICENSES/') emits 'LICENSES/<rel>'
rootCauses.workflowImpact: license-scan-shards jobs fail closed at the per-shard self-check (comm -3 shard_files.txt vs report_paths.txt is non-empty) and, failing that, the license-scan merge step fails its set-completeness check - the fail-closed safety net holds (no silent partial pass reaches adjudication), but the shard topology itself can never pass

rootCauses.title: ScanCode default-ignores .gitignore/.gitattributes (8 tracked files invisible in ANY topology)
rootCauses.measured: tracked 6576 vs full-scan file entries 6568: .gitattributes, .gitignore and 6 nested .gitignore files are never emitted; the pre-branch live report shows the same gap (6575 tracked -> 6567 files) - this gap predates the shard change and was invisible because the old topology never compared the scan surface to git ls-files
rootCauses.mechanism: commoncode/ignore.py ignores_VCS ('.gitignore', '.gitattributes': 'Default ignore: Git config artifact') - name-based default ignore applied in both '.'-scans and file-list scans
rootCauses.workflowImpact: even a correct shard implementation would fail the set-equality check (== git ls-files) by exactly these 8 files; the new completeness check is stricter than the scan surface the scanner can actually produce

rootCauses.title: branch's new epoch_record document triggers a denied-family GPL-3.0-only detection (independent of sharding)
rootCauses.measured: full.json evaluator verdict FAIL (exit 1): docs/evidence/epoch_record_pi_shard_2026-11-10.md -> gpl-3.0-only, 'neither declared (source-origin.yml) nor attributed (license-attribution.yml)', deniedFamily=true; the detection matches line 89 (negative-control prose naming the GPL-3.0 full-text file)
rootCauses.crossCheck: the other two branch-changed files carry only pre-existing, attributed detections (docs/spec/publication_integrity_gate.md composite expression and workflow 'JSON' - both present in the pre-branch live report with attribution entries at license-attribution.yml:166/192); the epoch record is absent from the live report (new file) and has no attribution entry
rootCauses.workflowImpact: even a fully corrected scan topology fails the license-scan dimension on this branch as committed - the old single-scan topology would fail identically; remediation (attribution entry vs document rewording vs rollback) is a main-agent decision, per protocol the data was not modified

metricsNote.filesScanned: full=7218 (files+dirs), merged=1303 (3 files + 650x2 duplicated dirs): the metric is files.len (publication_license_eval.nim:396) and includes directory entries; the verdict loop consumes only type=='file' entries (publication_license_eval.nim:310-312), so the metric difference is not a verdict input - but merged carries DUPLICATED directory entries because each shard report emits the full directory inventory and the jq merge concatenates both

commands: # 3. shard scans (workflow-identical xargs single-batch intent, run in parallel; nproc=16)

cd /tmp/j1-export && xargs -a /tmp/j1/shard0.txt /tmp/j1-venv/bin/scancode --license --copyright --processes 4 --json-pp /tmp/j1/shard0.json   # exit 0 but only 2 file entries (xargs split + include drop)
cd /tmp/j1-export && xargs -a /tmp/j1/shard1.txt /tmp/j1-venv/bin/scancode --license --copyright --processes 4 --json-pp /tmp/j1/shard1.json   # exit 0 but only 1 file entry
# 4. merge (workflow jq expression, verbatim from .github/workflows/publication-integrity.yml merge step)

jq -s '{headers: .[0].headers, files: (map(.files) | add | sort_by(.path)), license_detections: (map(.license_detections) | add | group_by(.identifier) | map(.[0] + {detection_count: (map(.detection_count) | add)}))}' /tmp/j1/shard0.json /tmp/j1/shard1.json > /tmp/j1/merged.json
# 5. set completeness (workflow semantics; PFX = basename of /tmp/j1-export)

/tmp/j1/vsi_license_eval --scan /tmp/j1/merged.json --policy compliance/policy/license-policy.yml --origin compliance/provenance/source-origin.yml --attribution compliance/provenance/license-attribution.yml --strip-prefix j1-export --out /tmp/j1/report_license_merged.json   # exit 0 PASS (vacuous, 3-file surface)

jq -S '<per-file signature projection: path(key) = license_detections[].license_expression_spdx|license_expression + detected_license_expression_spdx + copyrights holder/line sorted>' /tmp/j1/full.json > /tmp/j1/parity_baseline.json   # 6568 keys
